summary: Tech Lead for the Settlements team: sets technical direction for carrier payouts and reconciliation, stays hands-on in a NestJS and React codebase, and grows a team of six with a focus on correctness and scale.

prepNotes: Round: Imre Solvang, Manager Engineering; Tue Mar 3, 10:00-11:00 AT; leadership and experience deep dive, not coding; judges technical judgment, hands-on credibility, leadership, delivery judgment, operational ownership.

Tell me about yourself: 18 years; integration- and workflow-heavy platforms; freight and insurance at Quotewright and Saffron; now Larchmont Pay payments modernization; 50% implementation, 30% architecture, 20% mentoring.
Why Kestrel: direct domain fit (quoting, carrier integrations, payout workflows); a stack I want, PostgreSQL and NestJS; a role that stays hands-on with technical direction and mentoring.

Why Tech Lead: stay close to the code so decisions are grounded; multiply the team through standards and review; if every hard call still needs me after six months, I built a dependency, not a stronger team.

Proudest and most relevant project: Quotewright multi-carrier quoting; carrier adapters behind one contract; schema-driven forms; server-owned quote state; 9 weeks, 30% less front-end code, 20% quoting efficiency, about $2M impact.

Modernization, recent work, leadership: Larchmont Pay; seams around the legacy PHP monolith with Laravel, Node, NestJS and contracts, no rewrite; six mentored, two promoted; 75% less scaffolding; 30% fewer incidents.

NestJS: a delivery and composition framework, not the architecture. Nest owns transport, validation and wiring; the domain layer owns workflows, rules and state changes; no business logic in controllers.

Microservices and service boundaries: logical boundary first; extract only for independent deployment, team ownership or failure isolation; otherwise a modular monolith; never because the codebase is large.

MongoDB to PostgreSQL, data consistency: move only for a real problem (integrity, transactions); by bounded context; backfill, parity checks, shadow reads; one writer; reversible cutover. Proof: Copperleaf, 3M+ learners, near-zero drift.

Third-party integrations, carrier APIs: the partner's API is not our domain model; adapter boundary, deadlines, bounded retries, idempotency keys, circuit breaking, reconciliation, per-partner latency and failure metrics.

Observability and incidents: start from the customer workflow (quote, book, pay); traces across services; alerts on symptoms; as incident lead, evidence over speculation, two owned follow-ups rather than ten vague ones.

Security and testing: built in, not a checklist; least privilege, validation at boundaries; unit for rules, contract for adapters, e2e for key journeys. Proof: Saffron Mutual, 65% fewer vulnerabilities, 80% coverage.
Product, deadline pressure, technical debt: clarify the outcome and its date; cut scope before quality; never hide risk; rank debt by incidents, security exposure and delivery friction.
DORA, mentoring, disagreement: metrics are system signals, never a ranking of people; mentor by pairing, review, delegate. Disagree with explicit reasons, a decision owner, a written decision.

First 90 days and AI: 30 learn the workflows and incidents and ship a small fix; 60 own a slice; 90 lead one improvement. AI is an accelerator, not an authority: contracts and tests define correctness.
Answer shape: context, problem, my part, decision, trade-off, result, lesson; two minutes. Why leaving Larchmont Pay: proud of the work; want stronger senior peers and broader ownership.
